author: emily_dickinson
text:
In this verse, we see how the poet uses simple words and phrases to create a beautiful image of nature. The first line sets up the scene by mentioning "it," which creates an anticipation for what is to come next. Then comes the description of the flowers and animals that fill the meadow - from daisies to butterflies! Each word choice adds depth to the imagery; "clover" sounds soft while also suggesting movement with its association with "bees." As readers read these lines aloud, they can almost imagine themselves walking through such a field filled with life and color.

text:
A little girl was sitting on the edge of her bed, looking up at the moon through the window. She had been dreaming about all sorts of things that night: fairies dancing across the garden, talking animals coming out to play, and stories that would come alive around her. But now she couldn’t get any sleep. The moon looked so big and bright outside; it seemed as if it could reach right into the house with its light.

“I wish I were there,” thought the little girl, “just one more time.”
